findings.body: All AssignmentSource objects created in a long-running worker carry the identical process-start timestamp instead of the time the assignment was queued, making the `queued` field useless for staleness/loop-window checks and misleading in any serialized task payload or log.
findings.failure_mode: The `queued` timestamp is frozen at module import, so the recorded queue time is incorrect for every AssignmentSource created afterward.
findings.impact: All AssignmentSource objects created in a long-running worker carry the identical process-start timestamp instead of the time the assignment was queued, making the `queued` field useless for staleness/loop-window checks and misleading in any serialized task payload or log.
findings.root_cause: A callable's result was used as a dataclass field default, which Python evaluates a single time at class-definition (import) time.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so the timestamp is computed per instance.
findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time, so every instance shares the same stale timestamp
findings.trigger: Any code path that constructs an AssignmentSource without an explicit `queued` value, e.g. `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` in sync_group_assignee_inbound; the default `timezone.now()` is executed exactly once when the module is imported, not per instance.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 18 shows `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a dataclass field default. Python evaluates this once at class definition time, not per-instance. The patch introduces this bug; any AssignmentSource created without explicit queued will share the same stale timestamp.

pr.body:
## The problem:
When a Jira issue's `assignee` field is quickly modified multiple times in a row, we end up assigning and resyncing the assignees to Jira, which causes a loop. This is because _all_ inbound integration webhooks that modify an issue assignment generate an outbound update for all issue sync integrations as well.

## Solution:
This PR adds a new `AssignmentSource` dataclass, which acts as a context carrier when an external webhook triggers an issue assignment change. This is then checked on the outbound sync logic, preventing the change from being propagated to the same integration that initially triggered the change.
pr.title: fix(ecosystem): Breaks issue sync cycles

raw_findings.body: The abstract signature falsely suggests status syncs participate in the assignment-source cycle-break; implementers may rely on receiving assignment_source that is never supplied, and ExampleIntegration's `sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` would raise TypeError if any future caller does pass it.
raw_findings.failure_mode: API contract drift: signature advertises behavior that does not exist, creating a latent TypeError trap and reviewer confusion.
raw_findings.impact: The abstract signature falsely suggests status syncs participate in the assignment-source cycle-break; implementers may rely on receiving assignment_source that is never supplied, and ExampleIntegration's `sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` would raise TypeError if any future caller does pass it.
raw_findings.root_cause: A parameter relevant only to assignee syncing was added to the status-sync abstract method without wiring any caller or implementation to it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove `assignment_source` from the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature (assignment context is only relevant to assignee sync), or plumb it through the sync_status_outbound task and all subclass overrides consistently.
raw_findings.title: New `assignment_source` parameter on abstract sync_status_outbound is dead and misleading — the status sync task never passes it
raw_findings.trigger: Reading or extending the IssueSyncIntegration contract: `src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py` still calls `installation.sync_status_outbound(external_issue, ..., project_id)` with no assignment_source, and no subclass (jira, jira_server, vsts, example) declares or reads the parameter.

raw_findings.body: Under JSON task serialization the datetime either fails to serialize or arrives as an ISO string, which `AssignmentSource.from_dict` accepts unchecked, producing an ill-typed `queued: str` object; the payload also trips the bad-use-of-pickle complaint where enabled.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Task payload compatibility silently depends on pickle serialization; migrating to JSON breaks or corrupts the queued field.
raw_findings.impact: Under JSON task serialization the datetime either fails to serialize or arrives as an ISO string, which `AssignmentSource.from_dict` accepts unchecked, producing an ill-typed `queued: str` object; the payload also trips the bad-use-of-pickle complaint where enabled.
raw_findings.root_cause: AssignmentSource.to_dict emits a non-JSON-serializable datetime directly into cross-process task kwargs without an explicit wire encoding.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Serialize `queued` to an ISO-8601 string in `to_dict()` and parse it back to a datetime in `from_dict()` (or drop `queued` from the wire payload since it is unused by the cycle-break check).
raw_findings.title: Serializing a datetime (`queued`) into Celery task kwargs breaks JSON-serializable task-payload expectations
raw_findings.trigger: sync_group_assignee_outbound is invoked with an assignment_source; `to_dict()` (asdict) embeds the raw `queued: datetime` object into `apply_async(kwargs=...)`, which only round-trips because the codebase currently uses `CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle"` (with CELERY_COMPLAIN_ABOUT_BAD_USE_OF_PICKLE guarding non-JSON payloads).

validated_findings.trigger: The patch adds `assignment_source` plumbing to `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign` (used by sync_group_assignee_inbound's unassign branch), but the new tests only verify cycle-breaking for `assign` (test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration); the deassign test still asserts only `assignment_source=None`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap claim, not a code defect. The patch adds assignment_source to deassign but the candidate claims no test covers it. Test gaps are not bugs in the code itself. The category 'test_gap' confirms this is about missing tests, not broken functionality.
